talk: PE firms explain their returns with a value bridge: how much came from growing profit, how much from selling at a higher multiple, and how much from paying down debt. Growing profit is the part buyers trust most, and multiple expansion is partly luck.

terms.meaning: Making more profit than when you bought.
Selling at a higher multiple than you bought at.
Splitting a gain into growth, multiple and debt paydown.

questions.prompt: You bought a club at 8 times its $5M EBITDA. What did you pay?
whyNot: That adds the multiple to EBITDA. Multiply: $5M x 8 = $40M.
$5M x 10 = $50M uses a multiple of 10. You paid 8 times.

questions.prompt: Years later you sell at 10 times EBITDA, which has grown to $7M. What's it worth now?
questions.hint: New EBITDA times the new multiple.
whyNot: $7M x 8 = $56M uses the old multiple. You sold at 10 times.
$70M + $5M = $75M adds the old EBITDA on top. Value is just EBITDA times the multiple.

questions.prompt: The gain is $70M - $40M = $30M. How much of it came from growing EBITDA, valued at the old multiple of 8?
questions.hint: Extra EBITDA times the old multiple.
whyNot: $14M is the part from the higher multiple.
($7M - $5M) x 10 = $20M uses the exit multiple. Measure growth at the entry multiple.
$30M is the whole gain, growth and multiple together.

penalty.prompt: You bought at {m1} times EBITDA of {e1} and sold at {m2} times EBITDA of {e2}. How much of the gain came from growing EBITDA, measured at the entry multiple?
penalty.hint: Extra EBITDA times the entry multiple.
working: Bought at {e1} x {m1} = {e1 * m1|usd}. Sold at {e2} x {m2} = {e2 * m2|usd}.
The rest of the gain came from the higher multiple.

traps.why: That uses the exit multiple. Measure growth at the entry multiple, {m1}.
That's the whole gain, not just the growth part.

call.title: Where to focus before the sale
call.prompt: Your partners want to sell in two seasons. You could spend $2M modernising the shop and hospitality, adding $20,000 of profit a matchday. Or spend $2M on a PR campaign to excite buyers and hope for a higher multiple. Or cut the youth academy for $10,000 more profit a matchday now, losing about 1,000 fans later.

options.label: Modernise shop and hospitality
options.result: Good call. Real profit growth is the part of the bridge buyers trust and pay a multiple for.

options.label: PR campaign for a higher multiple
options.result: Buyers see through hype. The multiple mostly follows the market, not your marketing.

options.label: Cut the academy
options.result: Short-term profit up, fans down later. Buyers check the trend.

later.text: Without the academy, about 1,000 fans drift away.

takeaway: Returns come from growth, a better multiple and paying down debt. Growth is the one you control.
